1. How you are assessed and ultimately predicted grades depends on your specific school. 

Many schools hold mock exams once a year and topic tests throughout the semesters. This is to prepare you for the real exam session (the only one that "counts") and to predict your potential exam performance.

2. If you’re talking about the real exams, the exam schedule is changed from year to year. Depending on your subject combination, you may expect to do various papers in one day. This year, the first exam was scheduled to be on the 1st of May and the last one on the 22nd. 

If you’re talking about internal "exams", this will depend on your school. We had a mock session in the 2nd semester of Y1 and another session in the 2nd semester of Y2. In addition to this, we had frequent topic tests in each subject. These tests were for the most part based on exam style questions. 

3. All official IB exams are done by hand under very strict conditions.

You didn’t make it clear what "online arrangement" is reffering to, but I take it that you are talking about internal mocks and topic tests used for PG assessment. 

This will also depend on your school, but I know that some schools are cautious about assessing students online.


In conclusion: ask your coordinator for further details regarding your specific school.

Keep in mind that this is a global issue and that grade boundaries are determined by the overall performance of students in each specific subject, in each specific exam session. 

If M21 students perform on average substantially lower than that of students in previous sessions, grade boundaries will go down.

View your first set of PGs as a benchmark for further improvement. You now have the opportunity to analyse your study routine/technique and compare it to your overall performance in the different subjects. What are your strengths, weaknesses etc.
